simple.meaning: קָלַס (qâlaç) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to disparage , i.e. ridicule.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across 2 Kings, Ezekiel, Habakkuk, beginning at 2 Kings 2:23. Its contexts include kingship, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קָלַס (H7046).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: קָלַס (qâlaç) / H7046 is traced through 2 Kings 2:23, Ezekiel 16:31, Ezekiel 22:5, Habakkuk 1:10 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: He went up from there to Bethel. As he was going up by the way, some youths came out of the city and mocked him, and said to him, “Go up, you baldy! Go up, you baldy!”

definitions.full: H7046. qalas [ קָלַס ] verb mock, scoff (Ecclus 11:4 תקלס , text by Adler JQ xii (1900), 470 ); — Pi`el Infinitive construct אָתְנָן לְקַלֵּס Ezek 16:31 to scoff at hire (of Jerusalem under figure of harlot), but ᵑ6 ᵐ5 Symm collect , read לִקְבֹּץ Gr Toy Krae (or לְלַקֵּט , Co). Hithpa`el mock, deride , with ב person, Imperfect 3masculine singular יִתְקַלָּ֑ס Hab 1:10 ; 3 masculine plural יִתְקַלְּסוּ Ezek 22:5 , ׳וַיִּת 2Kin 2:23 .
